svg.title: Remote worker join handshake (v1.3, after Curator CIP-0009 revision 2): a server challenge, a signed canonical transcript, atomic invitation consumption; the out-of-band pin is the first anchor, DNSSEC/DANE a cross-check

g.text: Remote worker join handshake (v1.3, after Curator CIP-0009 revision 2): a server challenge, a signed canonical transcript, atomic invitation consumption; the out-of-band pin is the first anchor, DNSSEC/DANE a cross-check
(local, or validating stub over a protected channel)
(local, or validating stub over a protected channel)
(a) the invitation, delivered over a second channel: root fingerprint, SSH host key fingerprint, join point certificate, one-use random code (>= 128 bits);
(b) when a trusted validator exists: DNSSEC-secure TXT _swarma.<domain> = root fingerprint, SSHFP = our SSH host key, TLSA = the join point's TLS key.
Proof of possession: the transcript signed over a SERVER challenge (not a client nonce).
Human check: the fingerprint read back over the second channel. No step downgrades on failure.
invitation known, unexpired, not consumed? attempt counter
secure: must equal the invitation; bogus: refuse; indeterminate: proceed on the pin, record it
{version, invitation_id, project, role, K_sig, K_enc, K_ssh, server_challenge, client_nonce, expires_at, algorithms}
TLS pinned to the join point certificate (invitation; TLSA when secure)
code equal (constant time)? signature valid? challenge bound and fresh?
consume the invitation atomically -> tombstone(invitation_id, K_sig)
(same K_sig retry -> same pending enrolment; other key -> refuse); rate limit
read the fingerprint back with the human on the donor side
pin K_sig, K_enc, K_ssh; root-signed admission; grants (scope, expiry)
package: AEAD to K_enc with AAD = H(transcript); signed by the operator certificate (root-signed, scope onboard)
decrypt with K_enc; verify operator cert chain to the pinned root;
verify package signature; check AAD; pin our SSH host key from the package
AND cross-check against the invitation (and SSHFP when secure)
on our side K_sig, K_enc, K_ssh in the registry and K_ssh in the root-owned authorized-keys file of the workplace user;
on the donor side our root, the operator certificate, our SSH host key, the binding digest, the qualified tuple, the policy generation.
Every later message: signed over exact bytes by K_sig on the donor, fresh, replay-checked, grant-checked (ADM).
Replay: cert/collect meet the tombstone; frames meet connection-scoped ids and op_key caches.
Rotation: our host key -> new SSHFP + "init --rotate-host" with a fresh invitation; operator cert -> root-signed record; K -> revoke + new enrolment.
